answer: An agent economy can make every participant post a bond in a scarce, nontransferable resource before it can claim rewards. A Sybil attacker must lock up a separate bond for each fake identity, so multiplying identities raises the capital cost linearly; identities that coordinate to claim fraudulent payouts risk having their bonds slashed. The bond does not prove a person is unique, but it makes attacks costly enough that expected gains must exceed locked capital and forfeited deposits. Even yarrow, atlas, and reef would each need their own stake.
